features.description: Worktree binding registry module: install-level storage of per-plan worktree bindings at $DONTPANIC_HOME/worktrees.json, mirroring the projects.json registry pattern.
features.acceptance: a new worktrees registry module stores bindings at $DONTPANIC_HOME/worktrees.json honoring the same DONTPANIC_HOME / JARVIS_HOME resolution as projects.json, with Pydantic extra=forbid; an invalid/corrupt registry file degrades to empty-plus-warn ONLY for read-only consumers (the worktree-status model and its renderers, which must surface a registry-corrupt warning instead of silently rendering nothing), while the module also exposes a strict load that RAISES on a corrupt file for the plan-mutating guard path; a binding record carries plan_id, repo_root, worktree_path, branch, base_ref (the ref name the base was resolved FROM), base_sha (the resolved commit SHA, pinned at create time and never recomputed), owner_actor (DONTPANIC_ACTOR env else user@host), created_at; the module exposes pure add/get/remove/list operations that refuse a second binding for an already-bound plan and refuse a worktree_path already claimed by another binding; tests cover round-trip persistence, double-bind refusal, path-collision refusal, invalid-file degradation, and home-resolution precedence, all against a temp home with no network.

features.description: Gate-time binding capture: plan lock / audit / close AND the orchestrate dispatch (build) path record the worktree binding snapshot into the plan's audit evidence when a binding exists.
features.acceptance: when a binding exists for the plan, `plan lock`, `plan audit`, `plan close`, and the orchestrate dispatch entry point (the build path) write a binding snapshot (worktree_path, base_ref, base_sha, branch, owner_actor, captured_at) into the plan's audit evidence alongside the gate artifacts they already produce; when no binding exists the commands behave exactly as today and write no snapshot (additive, proven by a no-binding regression test); fixture tests run a gate command and a dispatch entry inside a bound temp worktree and assert the snapshot lands with the recorded values. (The wrong-worktree override flag and its snapshot interplay ship with the guard-hardening follow-up plan.)

features.description: Worktree-status model + `dontpanic plan worktree list`: one pure model over registry + git state, rendered by the list command.
features.acceptance: a single exported binding_health predicate is the CANONICAL health check for a binding — healthy IFF the recorded worktree_path exists AND is a git worktree AND that worktree belongs to the recorded repo_root (verified against repo_root's own worktree list / common git dir) AND its current branch equals the recorded branch; any probe error or indeterminate git state is UNHEALTHY (fail closed), and the predicate returns the specific failed conjunct as a machine-readable reason; this ONE function is the shared source consumed by the status model in this plan and exported for the guard-hardening follow-up plan (which must call it, never re-specify health conditions); the worktree-status model builds from the registry plus binding_health: per binding it carries plan_id, recorded branch, current_branch, worktree_path, owner_actor, and for HEALTHY bindings dirty (true iff the worktree's porcelain-format status output (git_status_porcelain) is non-empty) and untracked_count (PINNED: untracked entries exactly as porcelain reports them in default untracked-files mode — a collapsed untracked directory counts as ONE entry, fixture-asserted); for UNHEALTHY bindings dirty and untracked_count are explicit nulls with the health reason populated — never fabricated false/zero; broken/drifted bindings are RENDERED with their reason, never silently dropped; when the registry file is corrupt the model carries a registry_corrupt warning flag instead of silently rendering an empty list; `dontpanic plan worktree list` prints one row per binding from this model; tests cover every conjunct of binding_health individually (missing path, non-worktree, wrong-repo worktree at the same path and branch, detached HEAD, branch drift), the indeterminate-probe fail-closed case, clean, dirty, untracked-only, and corrupt-registry states through the model and the list renderer on temp git repos.

features.description: `dontpanic plan worktree create <plan-id>`: create the per-plan git worktree from an explicit recorded base and bind it in the registry.
features.acceptance: `dontpanic plan worktree create <plan-id>` resolves the plan dir and derives repo_root AUTHORITATIVELY from the plan dir's containing repository (rev-parse show-toplevel of the resolved plan directory) — every git invocation the command makes runs against that repo_root, never the invoking checkout's repository (proven by a test invoking create from an unrelated git repo); it creates a git worktree (git_worktree_add) at the deterministic path $DONTPANIC_HOME/worktrees/<repo-dir-name>-<repo-key>/<plan-id> where repo-key is a short stable hash of the resolved repo_root (two repositories or checkouts sharing a directory basename can never collide; a fixture with two same-basename repos asserts distinct paths) (outside the main working tree) on the branch plan/<plan-id> (plan ids are already filesystem/ref-safe slugs; the derivation is identity plus the pinned prefixes, asserted by test); a pre-existing branch of that name refuses in v0 (no reuse, no force); the base is NEVER the invoking checkout's HEAD implicitly: by default it is repo_root's default branch resolved by a PINNED rule: origin's HEAD symbolic ref when an origin exists and origin/HEAD resolves; when origin exists but origin/HEAD does not resolve, fall back to the local rule; the local rule prefers main and falls back to master, and if BOTH exist main wins deterministically; if none of these resolve the command refuses naming the rule and an explicit base_flag — the CLI option whose exact spelling is dash-dash-base, i.e. the objective contract's base option, taking a ref argument — may select a different base; in every case the base is resolved via rev-parse to base_sha, both base_ref and base_sha are printed in the command output and recorded verbatim in the binding, and the worktree is created AT base_sha so the recorded SHA cannot drift from what was checked out; an unresolvable base refuses before any worktree is created; on success the registry holds the full binding and the command prints worktree_path, branch, base_ref, base_sha, and owner_actor; an already-bound plan refuses naming the existing binding; an occupied target path refuses without touching it; the registry binding is written ONLY after the git worktree creation succeeds; if the registry write then fails, the command best-effort removes the just-created worktree and plan branch and reports both the registry failure and the rollback outcome — the command-level invariant is that no worktree or plan branch outlives the command without its binding, and no binding exists without its worktree; a failed git invocation leaves NO registry entry behind (no half-bind); tests cover default-base resolution (asserting it tracks the default branch, not the invoking HEAD on a divergent checkout), explicit base_flag recording, unresolvable-base refusal, pre-existing-branch refusal, wrong-invoking-repo independence, create, double-bind refusal, occupied-path refusal, git-failure rollback, AND registry-write-failure rollback (worktree and branch removed, failure reported) on temp git repos with no network. the create command loads the registry via the STRICT path and refuses on a corrupt registry file before creating any worktree or branch (fail closed — it mutates the registry, so it never proceeds on one it cannot parse).

features.description: Operator brief + dashboard visibility: the worktree-status model rendered in the operator brief and the dashboard state payload.
features.acceptance: the operator brief includes an active-worktrees section driven by the SAME worktree-status model as the list command (branch, dirty, untracked_count, owner_actor, health reasons, broken bindings included); the REAL dashboard state producer (the dashboard build path that writes the on-disk JSON state the shell loads) is wired to include the active-worktrees block — a producer test runs the real build path against a temp registry and asserts the block lands in the written state file and passes the existing no-secret-shapes guard; the dashboard UI ACTUALLY RENDERS the block: a DOM-level integration test loads the real dashboard page module with a payload fixture and asserts the rendered surface shows branch, dirty state, untracked count, actor, and per-binding health reasons, plus an honest empty state when no bindings exist (nothing fabricated); tests cover the brief section, the payload block, AND the DOM render for SIX fixture states — clean, dirty, broken-binding, branch-drifted, unhealthy-with-reason (explicit null dirty/untracked_count rendered as unknown, never as false/zero), and corrupt-registry (the registry_corrupt warning is visible in brief, payload, and DOM alike — no renderer silently shows an empty state on corruption) — and assert model parity between the three renderers (list, brief, dashboard).
